_comment: Relic plaque text for the Keeping Room. This file is WRITING, not balance - it deliberately contains no spawn rates, values or weights, so nothing in it is Chris's to tune. Add those elsewhere.
_rules: Two sentences. Never three. About a person, not about the world. Never explain a mechanic - a plaque is not a tutorial. Some are unknown and stay unknown: the order's earliest records burned long before any storm, and nothing brought back from a run will fill that shelf. See docs/HOW-THE-PLAYER-LEARNS.md.
_howItReads: A relic is the lantern-only loot tier, so it costs a real decision to find one. Hand it in at a plinth and it gets named. That is the whole lore-delivery system: the risky choice is the only way to learn what happened here.

relics.name: Counter lanyard, laminated
relics.text: Teodora ran the pretzel counter for nine years and was proud of never once calling in sick. The morning of the storm she finally did.

relics.name: Ledger, water-swollen
relics.text: Somebody kept writing in the back of this after the registers died. The last page is a list of who still had insulin.

relics.name: Ring, still boxed
relics.text: Bought on layaway: eleven payments of forty dollars, each one initialled. The twelfth was due the week the sky went out.

relics.name: Pedometer, strap perished
relics.text: Harold walked four laps of the upper floor every morning before the shops opened. It reads two thousand eight hundred and forty-seven miles.

relics.name: Child's drawing, taped
relics.text: A house, a dog, and four stick figures under a hard yellow sun. We have never worked out which cashier taped it inside her drawer.

relics.name: Arcade tokens, six hundred
relics.text: Worth nothing outside this building then, and nothing anywhere now. Someone in the order counted all six hundred anyway, and wrote the number down.

relics.name: Security handset
relics.text: It still cycles through the night door-checks on a loop, in order, politely. Nobody has managed to switch it off and nobody has quite wanted to.

relics.name: Unknown
relics.text: Recovered from the first hall after the water went down. Whatever its label said, the fire had already taken it.

relics.name: Swimming badge, 25 yards
relics.text: Sewn on, picked off, and kept in a wallet for forty years. The valley has flooded three times and somebody here learned to swim late.

relics.name: Shift rota, laminated
relics.text: Twenty-two names, and beside four of them somebody has pencilled a small tick. We do not know what the ticks meant and we no longer ask.

relics.name: Incline ticket, unpunched
relics.text: A return fare up the hill, bought and never used. Whoever held it chose to stay down in the valley that day.

relics.name: Works badge, number 4471
relics.text: His grandfather poured steel, his father poured steel, and he sold shoes on the upper floor. He kept the badge in his till all the same.

relics.name: Unknown
relics.text: The card beneath it survived and reads only a date. Everything that date referred to burned with the rest.

relics.name: Photo strip, four frames
relics.text: Two girls, aged about fifteen, getting progressively less serious. Somebody tore it down the middle and kept both halves.

relics.name: Ladle, handle rewrapped
relics.text: It was rewrapped with tape four separate times rather than replaced. The Good Cheer Club uses it at the long table most evenings.

relics.name: Lost child card, blank
relics.text: The top of the pad, never filled in, from a stack of a hundred. Every card under it had been used.

relics.name: Lens, hand-ground
relics.text: Ground by somebody who had done it a long time and was in no hurry. Three of the order's lanterns still carry lenses from this counter.

relics.name: Unknown
relics.text: Small, heavy, and nobody living has ever known what it is. It is kept on the shelf because it was kept on the shelf.

relics.name: Mug, chipped at the lip
relics.text: Marguerite's, and everyone knew it was Marguerite's, and nobody else used it. She carried it home in her coat pocket for thirty years and then back again.

relics.name: Closing notice, unposted
relics.text: Printed, signed, and never put up in the window. The storm closed the store eleven days before the company meant to.
